The ideal candidate brings strong market knowledge, a proven sales track record in premium real estate, and the ability to build lasting relationships with HNW/UHNW clients, brokers, and key partners. Develop, activate, and manage a high-performing broker and channel partner network across the UK and European markets. Build strong relationships with property consultancies, wealth advisors, real estate agencies, and referral partners to generate qualified sales opportunities. Execute market expansion strategies focused on London, Manchester, Birmingham, and other key target locations. Conduct regular broker meetings, training sessions, project presentations, webinars, and roadshows to increase market awareness and engagement. Collaborate closely with Sales and Marketing teams to align lead generation campaigns, events, and promotional activities. Monitor broker performance, pipeline progression, and conversion metrics, ensuring timely follow-up and reporting. Represent the company at international property exhibitions, networking events, and investor forums. Gather market intelligence on competitor activity, customer preferences, and emerging opportunities within the UK and European real estate investment landscape. Maintain accurate records of broker engagement, opportunities, and business development activities within the CRM system. Support sales conversion efforts by coordinating introductions, client meetings, and investment presentations. Highly professional, entrepreneurial, and commercially focused with excellent communication and presentation skills. If you have what it takes to sell extraordinary homes and create an exceptional buyer journey, click Apply and be part of Amali’s story in shaping luxury living.

review_candidates.title: Executive Secretary, Malabo Equatorial Guinea - G5
review_candidates.description: The Position JOB DESCRIPTION Under the direct guidance and supervision of the UNFPA Representative in Equatorial Guinea, the Executive Assistant to the Representative's Office provides administrative and secretarial support, maintaining the strictest confidentiality in all aspects of their duties. The incumbent ensures adherence to protocol procedures, manages the flow of information, and monitors deadlines and commitments. How You Can Make a Difference UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person's potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies. In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction. UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results Job Purpose The incumbent will provide high-level communication, administrative, and secretarial support to the Representative (and, where applicable, the Deputy Representative). In close collaboration with the office team, the Executive Assistant will organize the functions of the Representative's office to ensure an effective communication flow, facilitate knowledge management, and provide logistical and coordination support. You Would Be Responsible For Communication and Administrative Support Ensure an optimal communication flow between the Representative's Office, country office staff in Malabo (and other sub-offices if applicable), Headquarters, and external counterparts, through the effective use of written, verbal, and electronic communication. Register and channel incoming documents addressed to the Representative for staff action. Review and ensure compliance with UNFPA guidelines and procedures for all outgoing correspondence before submission for signature. Draft non-substantive correspondence, take dictation, and prepare letters, documents, and memoranda, exercising a quality control function for all outgoing documents (format, grammar, and style). Respond to requests for information—potentially confidential—in a timely, discreet, and accurate manner. Prepare, process, and classify confidencial information. Assist in the overall administration of the Representative's Office; coordinate and monitor diverse activities and work processes to ensure that management directives are properly executed and products are delivered on time. Coordination and Support Take full responsibility for time management and schedule planning on behalf of the Representative, with prior consultation. Make arrangements, provide supporting documentation, and follow up on meetings for the Representative. Take minutes or notes as required during meetings. Screen and prioritize all incoming correspondence; compile relevant reference documents; identify matters requiring the Representative's attention and route others to appropriate officers; follow up on actions to be taken. Manage protocol matters and receive high-ranking visitors/officials (Government, Diplomatic Corps, UN System in Equatorial Guinea). Logistics and Information Management Research files, compile requested information, and organize materials (summaries, reports, and reference documentation) for official missions and special meetings. Prepare briefing materials and presentations (e.g., PowerPoint) for the Representative. Facilitate logistical, administrative, and financial preparations for meetings and workshops attended by the Representative. Establish and maintain filing and tracking systems for the Representative's Office. Arrange travel for the Representative, prepare mission folders, and manage mission reports. Manage attendance and leave records for the Representative's Office. Other Duties Assist in the preparation and finalization of the Office's Annual Work Plan. Provide informal translations and act as an interpreter when necessary (particularly given the multilingual environment of Equatorial Guinea). Perform any other duties required by the Office Management. Education Qualifications and Experience: Completion of secondary education is required. A first-level university degree will be considered an asset. Knowledge And Experience Minimum of five (5) years of experience providing specialized administrative support to a senior executive, with experience in finance and administration. Previous experience in research support and data management. Previous experience in the United Nations and knowledge of diplomatic protocols will be considered an asset. Strong interpersonal and organizational skills. Proficiency in computer applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.). Strong drafting and communication skills. Initiative, sound judgment, interest in development work (especially UNFPA's mission), and dedication to the principles of the United Nations. Languages Fluency in Spanish and English (oral, written, and reading) is required. Knowledge of French is considered a strong asset. Values Required Competencies: Exemplifying integrity, Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system, Embracing cultural diversity, Embracing change Core Competencies Achieving results, Being accountable, Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen, Thinking analytically and strategically, Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships Functional Competencies Providing administrative/logistical support to the executive direction. Managing documents, correspondence, and reports. Planning, organizing, and multitasking. Managing information and workflow. Compensation And Benefits This position offers an attractive remuneration package including a competitive net salary plus health insurance and other benefits as applicable. UNFPA Work Environment UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA's workforce - click here to learn more. Disclaimer Selection and appointment may be subject to background and reference checks, medical clearance, visa issuance and other administrative requirements. UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants' bank accounts. Applicants for positions in the international Professional and higher categories, who hold permanent resident status in a country other than their country of nationality, may be required to renounce such status upon their appointment.

Ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with contract requirements, technical standards, and client expectations. Establish and enforce consistent construction management standards, processes, and KPIs across the DER portfolio. Lead construction execution for EPC, Design-Build, and fixed-price projects, including self-perform and subcontracted scopes. Oversee construction planning, mobilization, execution, commissioning, and turnover activities across multiple regions. Ensure effective integration between engineering, procurement, and construction functions to support predictable project delivery. Drive continuous improvement in construction productivity, cost control, schedule performance, and risk management. Serve as a visible safety leader and champion a zero-incident culture across all DER construction activities. Partner with McKinstry Safety and Quality teams to ensure compliance with all OSHA, site-specific, and client safety requirements. Ensure quality management plans are implemented and adhered to across all projects. Lead root cause analysis and corrective actions for safety incidents, quality issues, and near misses. Ensure commissioning, testing, and turnover processes meet contractual, regulatory, and client standards. Maintain project portfolio financial accountability for construction execution performance, including cost forecasting, margin protection, and change management. Ensure disciplined change order management and claims mitigation. Support accurate forecasting and reporting to executive leadership. Build scalable construction teams capable of delivering complex, multi-site and utility-scale DER projects nationally. Set clear performance expectations and hold teams accountable to McKinstry values and operational standards. Foster collaboration across construction, engineering, development, and supply chain teams. Support workforce planning aligned with projected growth in DER markets. Serve as an executive point of contact for key IPP, C&I, and utility clients during construction execution. Build and maintain trusted client relationships through proactive communication and issue resolution. Partner with Development, Sales, and Estimating teams during pursuit, preconstruction, and contract negotiations. The following organisations are also eligible for observer status within GlASA: the Central Banks of Signatory States, regional Securities and Exchange Commissions, UEMOA, Banque Ouest Africaine pour Le Developpement, (BOAD) the French Zone Anti-Money Laundering Liaison Committee (Conseil Regional de I’Epargne Public et des Marches Financiers), the African Development Bank (ADB), the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the FATF, Interpol, WCO, the Commonwealth Secretariat, and the European Union. In 2007, Observer status was granted to the Egmont Group and the Republic of Sao Tome and Principe. The Organs Of GlASA Are The Ad-hoc Ministerial Committee; The Administrative Secretariat; The Technical Commission; The Network of National Correspondents. Role Overview The deputy Director General is selected on the basis of personal leadership skills, experience, and competence, and is appointed for a non-renewable period of 4 years. He/She is essentially a member of a team which provides leadership at a political and technical level in order to advance the agreed work of GlASA within its specialised areas. The Deputy Director General assists the Director General of GlASA in carrying out his/her role and deputies in his/her absence. Role And Responsibilities Under the guidance of the Director General and in harmony with colleagues, the other Organs of GIABA and the ECOWAS Commission, Assisting the Director General in the definition and implementation of GIABA’s strategy; Ensuring continuity in the organisation in the absence of the Director General and assisting the latter in carrying out his/her duties within the framework of GIABA’s Mission; Supervising the activities of directorates under him/her; Collaborating with his/her counterpart from other regional and international Bodies; Assists the Director General to prepare interim and annual reports which shall be submitted to the ECOWAS Authorities by the President of the Commission; Assists in the Implementation of annual work programme of GIABA; Assists and deputises for the Director General in the execution of all his/her duties; Discharges all duties assigned to him/her by the Director General; Collaborates with other regional international bodies, specialised institutions, public-private partnerships to facilitate the implementation of regional programmes; Collaborates and works in synergy with colleagues and organs of GIABA. In addition to the functions listed above, the Deputy Director General is expected, among other things, to communicate a compelling vision of GIABA’s role in integration programmes and ensure that staff and stakeholders subscribe to and support that vision. The Deputy Director General is also responsible for leading and managing the directors and staff, under his/her authority, which includes: Ensuring that he/she remains a successful team player within the Institution by contributing to common goals, assuming a fair share of the work, supporting fellow Heads of Institution in their own initiatives, and making enough time to meet with them on regular basis to discuss common concerns; Organising the staff under his/her authority efficiently, with clear reporting lines, definition of responsibilities; Ensuring that during his/her absence, an officer in-charge is thoroughly briefed and given the delegated authority to make decisions so that the work of the Institution is not obstructed. What the work involves: Flying BVLOS missions as remote pilot, including pre-flight inspections, launch, monitoring and recovery Ground operations at launch and landing sites, including payload handling and site setup Mission planning, route validation and contingency site work Routine maintenance and first-line troubleshooting Occasional liaison with customers, site partners and regulators Domestic travel across our Romanian sites, with opportunities to support our international operations We are growing. You ask early when something is unclear instead of guessing. You write things down so a colleague in Bali or Brisbane can pick them up without a phone call. Ownership. You prepare properly and follow work through to the end without being chased. When you spot a problem you raise it early, with options attached. Delivery. You work reliably, to standard, on time. Checklists, cross-checks and standard practice, every time, including when it is inconvenient Curiosity about how the system actually works, and the willingness to test the things everyone assumes are working Comfort with ambiguity and change. review_candidates.title: Asset Management Specialist
review_candidates.description: This position is on-site based in Damascus Governorate, Syria. Position Objective: Support the asset management workstream by capturing, validating, updating, and reconciling asset records from field surveys, inventory systems, asset registers, and implementation evidence in accordance with agreed standards. Job Description & Responsibilities: Capture and maintain asset records including site, room, row, rack, shelf, slot, card, port, serial number, model, vendor, tag, status, and evidence references. Validate physical survey outputs against inventory, CMDB, asset registers, and implementation/as-built documentation. Identify and report missing, duplicate, inconsistent, untagged, misplaced, or unknown assets. Apply agreed naming conventions, tagging rules, mandatory field requirements, lifecycle statuses, and data-entry standards. Prepare clean upload templates, discrepancy lists, evidence packs, and progress reports for SME review. Coordinate with field technicians, site teams, inventory specialists, and operations teams to resolve asset record gaps. Support asset movement, assignment, decommissioning, retirement, and reconciliation activities where required. Maintain traceability of data changes and ensure records are audit-ready. Follow site access, safety, confidentiality, and quality rules while handling asset information. Languages: English – mandatory Arabic – mandatory Position KPIs Asset records captured/validated per day against target. Data entry accuracy and first-pass acceptance rate. Completeness of mandatory asset attributes. Discrepancy reporting and closure support rate. Compliance with tagging, evidence, and lifecycle status standards. Qualifications & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Telecom or IT or equivalent. 5+ years in telecom asset management, physical inventory, CMDB/ITAM data operations, network records, or field survey support. Good understanding of telecom/network equipment, racks, shelves, cards, ports, labels, serial numbers, and site location hierarchy. Experience using Excel, structured templates, barcode/QR scanning tools, CMDB/ITAM/inventory systems, or mobile survey tools. Detail-oriented with the ability to follow data standards and escalate discrepancies clearly. Able to work with field teams and maintain accurate records under delivery timelines. Relevant Certificates: ITIL Foundation preferred ISO 55000 awareness preferred CMDB/ITAM platform training is an advantage
